_comment: Single source of truth for statutory fees and caps cited across the site. Every figure here is verified against a primary source. If a fee changes, change it HERE and re-run scripts/check_statutory_fees.py to find every page that still carries the old value. Do not hard-code these numbers into new pages without adding them here first.
_verified_by: Claude Code, against gov.uk / legislation.gov.uk primary sources

winding_up_petition_court_fee.description: Court fee for entering a winding-up petition (companies only).

winding_up_petition_deposit.description: Petition deposit payable to the Insolvency Service on a winding-up petition (other than under s.124A).

strike_off_ds01_online.description: Companies House fee to apply for voluntary strike-off (DS01) online.

strike_off_ds01_paper.description: Companies House fee to apply for voluntary strike-off (DS01) by paper.

statutory_weekly_pay_cap.description: Statutory weekly pay cap used for redundancy, arrears, notice and holiday pay claims. Effective 6 April 2026.

statutory_redundancy_maximum.description: Maximum statutory redundancy payment (£751 weekly cap x 30 weeks).
statutory_redundancy_maximum.source_name: Derived from the statutory weekly pay cap

_commercial_fees_comment: NOT statutory. These are Company Debt's own prices, so they are not verifiable against gov.uk. They are here because they drifted just as badly: the CVL fee was published as £4,000-£6,000 on four pages and £4,000-£7,000 on another, and disbursements as both £500-£1,000 and £500-£1,500. Owner set the canonical values on 2026-07-14.

cvl_practitioner_fee.description: Company Debt CVL practitioner fee, plus VAT, standard fixed fee for a straightforward case. Changed from a £4,000-£7,000 range to a flat £3,500 on 2026-07-15 (owner). Note: £4,000-£5,000 is NOT a drift pattern here - it is the current all-in figure (see cvl_all_in).

cvl_disbursements.description: Bond, Gazette notices, Companies House filing, statutory mailings.

cvl_all_in.description: Derived: £3,500 fixed fee + £500-£1,500 disbursements. Was £5,000-£9,000 when the fee was a £4,000-£7,000 range.

mvl_practitioner_fee.description: Company Debt MVL practitioner fee, plus VAT, standard fixed fee for a solvent company. Changed from a £2,000-£4,000 range to a flat £3,500 on 2026-07-15 (owner).

preferential_wages_limit.description: Per-employee limit on preferential status for arrears of wages in an insolvency.

_banned_claims._comment: Figures that must NOT appear anywhere on the site. Each was traced to an unverifiable origin. scripts/check_statutory_fees.py fails any page containing them.

director_redundancy_average._note: Regex, not literals: the claim appears in several phrasings and a literal list missed most of them. Two tiers, because £9,000 also legitimately appears as the top of the CVL all-in cost range (£5,000 to £9,000). banned_patterns are unambiguous and fire anywhere. banned_patterns_in_context are loose and only fire near a redundancy/claim word, so they do not flag a genuine cost figure.
director_redundancy_average.reason: Presented as an average successful director redundancy claim, but not supported by the cited gov.uk guidance. Traced to editorial-os/17-audience-and-persona.md and to Gemini research output, not to Company Debt caseload. Owner confirmed on 2026-07-14 that the firm cannot stand behind it.
director_redundancy_average.use_instead: The statutory calculation method (age, length of service, weekly pay), the £751 weekly cap, the £22,530 maximum, and a link to https://www.gov.uk/calculate-your-redundancy-pay so the reader gets their own figure.
